_README: Preregistered decision thresholds. Required by RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 7:
'commit the following to a timestamped file ... writing it after seeing the result
Every entry here must be committed BEFORE the run it judges. The git history is the
evidence of that ordering, and it is the only real protection: the same author writes
both the experiment and its kill condition, so no file permission makes this honest.
What a commit buys is that moving a threshold becomes a visible diff instead of a
Each threshold carries a derivation. A threshold without one is an arbitrary constant
wearing a harness, and an examiner's first question is 'who chose this number'.

C-6.name: Held-out probe pool
C-6.question: Are the published pilot metrics training metrics rather than generalization metrics?
background: Every metric in the project is computed on the same 4,096-point pool the chain trains
on. At B = 4096 the students train on all of it, so the tau0.5/1.0/2.0_b4096 rows of
the pilot table are training metrics by construction. Three of those rows are cited
as evidence in the public README.
C-6.metric: abs(agree_gen0 on probe pool - agree_gen0 on training pool) at generation 25
C-6.fails_if: metric exceeds threshold in any condition
derivation: Published generation-25 agreements at B = 4096 are 0.219, 0.164 and 0.132 for
tau = 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0. Adjacent conditions are separated by 0.055 and 0.032.
A probe-versus-training gap of 0.05 is therefore the scale at which the temperature
ordering could reorder - that is, the scale at which a stated conclusion changes.
Anything smaller moves numbers without moving claims.
verdict_if_failed: The published pilot table is a table of training metrics. Relabel it as such, and
rerun on the probe pool before any claim rests on those rows.
sanity_check: At B = 128 the students train on 128 of 4,096 points, so training-pool and probe-pool
metrics should already agree closely. A large gap THERE means the probe pool is built
wrong, not that the finding is real.

C-2.name: No chaining
C-2.question: Does iteration do anything that a single distillation step does not?
background: No control has ever compared a chain generation against a student distilled once
directly from generation 0. If chain-generation 5 looks like a fresh one-step
student, iteration is doing nothing and 'iterated distillation' is the wrong
description of the entire project.
C-2.reference_distribution: one-step students distilled directly from generation 0 at the same bottleneck

sanity.condition: chain-generation 1 lies inside the one-step reference's central 95%
sanity.meaning_if_failed: the control is misconfigured, not a finding - generation 1 IS a one-step student by construction

A.condition: some generation g <= 25 falls below the one-step reference's 2.5th percentile
A.meaning_if_failed: iteration changes nothing about the learned function

B.condition: some generation g <= 25 falls below the one-step reference's 2.5th percentile
B.meaning_if_failed: alphabet contraction is a one-step effect, not an iterated one

derivation: The 2.5th percentile is the one-sided form of the two-sided 95% intervals already
used in analysis/seed_stability_stats.py. It is the repository's existing statistical
convention rather than a new number introduced for this control.
verdict_if_failed: If gates A and B BOTH fail: hard stop. Iteration is doing nothing measurable, the
iterated framing is unsupported, and the semester's spine needs rethinking before any
further code is written.
If gate B alone fails: the contraction headline has a one-step explanation, and
C-4's minority-collapse concern (Fang et al. 2021, PNAS) arrives early. At B = 128
a one-step student already sees only about 2.6 examples per class.

C-3.name: One-step fidelity baseline
C-3.question: Is the loss from a single distillation step an optimization artifact or an information limit?
background: RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 4.1 specifies C-3 as agreement with generation 0 after a
SINGLE distillation step at B = 4096, and says: 'whatever that number is, it is the
floor against which all downstream decay must be read.'
C-2 already measured the number: 0.230 on held-out inputs at B = 4096, over 50
one-step students at 1500 training steps. So the floor exists. What C-2 did not
test is whether that floor MOVES with the training budget.
This matters because Stanton et al. attribute one-step teacher-student discrepancy
to optimization rather than information loss. If they are right here, the floor is a
property of how long we train, not of what the bottleneck destroys, and every decay
number in this project has been read against a budget-dependent baseline without
anyone saying so.
C-3.metric: one-step agree_gen0 at B = 4096 on the held-out probe pool, as training steps increase from the standard 1500
C-3.reference_provenance: logs/c2_no_chaining.json, 50 one-step students at 1500 steps, probe pool, 95% CI
C-3.fails_if: one-step agreement at 4x the training budget (6000 steps) exceeds 0.243, the upper bound of the 1500-step reference interval
derivation: The threshold is the upper bound of the measured reference interval, not a chosen
number. Run-to-run spread across 50 one-step students at the standard budget is
0.022 wide. A budget increase that pushes the mean outside that interval has moved
the floor by more than the noise it was measured with; one that does not, has not.
4x is the smallest multiplier that clearly separates a real trend from noise at this
interval width, and 6000 steps is about 11 s per student on this machine, so the
sweep is affordable at n = 20 per budget.
verdict_if_failed: The one-step floor is optimization-dependent, not an information limit. Consequences:
every decay claim must be reported against a budget-matched floor rather than against
generation 0 alone; the 1500-step choice becomes a reported parameter rather than an
implementation detail; and the C-2 escape generations (4, 7, 16) need re-checking,
since they are defined relative to a reference distribution that itself moves.
This does not invalidate C-2 — the chain still leaves the reference — but it changes
what the reference means.
verdict_if_passed: The floor is an information limit at this budget. 0.230 stands as the number all
downstream decay is read against, and the 1500-step choice is not load-bearing.
sanity_check: The 1500-step arm of this sweep must reproduce the C-2 reference mean of 0.230 within
its interval. If it does not, the sweep is not measuring the same thing C-2 measured
and nothing else in it can be read.

C-4.name: Matched imbalance — does soft-logit transmission starve classes?
C-4.question: Is alphabet contraction explained by minority collapse under class imbalance in the transmitted set, rather than by anything iteration does?
background: At B = 128 over 50 classes the transmitted set averages 2.56 examples per class.
Fang, He, Long and Su (PNAS 2021) characterize minority collapse analytically in
exactly that regime: as the ratio of majority to minority counts grows, the minority
classes' classifier vectors converge and those classes stop being predicted. That is
a competing explanation for this project's headline result, and it arrives with a
PNAS citation attached.
Their theory is written in per-class example counts, which a hard-label channel has
and a soft-logit channel does not. The transmitted object here is a matrix of
probabilities, so the corresponding quantity is the effective count: the column sum
of the transmitted softmax over the B selected inputs.
RESEARCH-PLAN section 4.1 allows C-4 to be answered either by constructing a
matched-imbalance control or by establishing that soft-logit transmission places mass
on all classes and therefore evades the mechanism. This entry judges the second route,
which costs five short chains rather than a new experimental arm. It can only close
the question or declare the first route mandatory; it cannot substitute for it.
C-4.metric: effective per-class count m_k(g) = sum over the B transmitted inputs of the teacher's softmax probability for class k, at tau = 1.0 and B = 128

A.condition: no class falls below one effective example at the first transmission
A.meaning_if_failed: soft transmission starves classes from the founder onward, so Fang's regime is entered before any chaining and the evasion route is closed

B.metric: overlap coefficient between the classes starved at generation 1 and the classes absent from generation 25's predictions, pooled over five chains
B.condition: the overlap does not exceed a permutation null that reassigns which classes are starved at matched set size
B.meaning_if_failed: which classes are starved predicts which classes die, so minority collapse is a live explanation for alphabet contraction and the constructed matched-imbalance control becomes mandatory

derivation: The 1.0 cutoff in gate A is not chosen, it is the unit Fang et al.'s theory is written
in. Their counts are whole labelled examples and n_min = 1 is the smallest count above
collapse, so a class receiving less soft mass than one hard example is inside their
regime by their own units rather than by a constant of mine.
The 0.05 in gate B is the repository's existing convention rather than a new number:
analysis/seed_stability_stats.py already tests survivor-set overlap against a
permutation null at that level, and gate B is the same statistic computed on a
different pair of sets. The overlap coefficient is used rather than Jaccard because
the two sets have systematically different sizes, which RESEARCH-PLAN section 4.3
records as a known defect of Jaccard in this project.
verdict_if_failed: If gate A alone fails: the evasion route is closed but nothing is yet explained.
Starvation exists; gate B is what says whether it matters.
If gate B fails: minority collapse is a live competing explanation for the project's
best result. The constructed matched-imbalance control becomes mandatory, and until it
runs the contraction claim must be stated with this explanation named and unexcluded.
If both fail: report alphabet contraction as consistent with minority collapse, and
stop describing it as a property of iterated transmission until the constructed
control separates the two.
verdict_if_passed: Soft-logit transmission feeds every class above the unit Fang et al.'s analysis is
written in, and starvation does not predict death. The minority-collapse explanation
is excluded for the soft arm without constructing a matched-imbalance control, and
C-4 is answered by the second route RESEARCH-PLAN section 4.1 allows.
sanity_check: The same measurement under argmax transmission at B = 128 must show classes at an
effective count of exactly zero, since a hard channel either selects a class or does
not. If the argmax arm shows no starved classes, the measurement is wrong rather than
the soft result surprising.

C-1.name: Shuffled transmission, replication at n = 20
C-1.question: Does the protective effect of intact input-to-target pairing survive a twentyfold sample?
background: C-1 ran on 2026-09-14 at three seeds per arm and is the one control in this project
with no committed gate: its decision rule is an inline 1.25 constant in
controls/c1_shuffled.py, added in the same commit as the control itself.
analysis/consistency_checks.py flags exactly this, and it is the only outstanding
finding of its kind.
This entry does not pretend to be a preregistration of an unseen result. The n = 3
outcome is already known and published in two progress reports: 11.3 surviving
classes intact against 1.3 shuffled, quoted as protection 'by roughly a factor of
nine'. What is preregistered here is the rule for judging the REPLICATION at n = 20,
written before those twenty chains per arm exist. It supersedes the inline 1.25
constant, which is retired.
C-1.metric: mean surviving classes at generation 25, intact arm against shuffled arm, 20 chains per arm at tau = 1.0 and B = 128

A.metric: ratio of intact-arm mean surviving classes to shuffled-arm mean
A.condition: the ratio is at least 3.0 at n = 20
A.meaning_if_failed: the protective effect does not survive the larger sample and the claim is withdrawn, not merely rescaled

B.metric: 95% bootstrap intervals of the two arm means, resampling chains
B.condition: the two intervals do not overlap
B.meaning_if_failed: the separation is not resolvable at n = 20 and the claim must be stated as unresolved rather than as a factor

derivation: Gate A is set at 3.0 against an observed 8.7x precisely so that it is not rigged to
pass. Effect sizes in this project shrink when the sample grows — the seed-stability
rerun took 2.94x down to 2.12x at the same fourfold increase — so a replication gate
set at the observed magnitude would fail for the wrong reason, punishing the known
small-sample inflation rather than testing whether the effect is real. 3.0 is the
level at which 'intact pairing protects the alphabet' remains a true sentence.
Gate B uses the bootstrap over chains introduced in analysis/seed_stability_stats.py,
which is the repository's existing convention: resampling is over chains rather than
over pairs, because the pairwise quantities are not independent.
verdict_if_failed: The nine-fold protection figure is withdrawn from README.md, progress-report-2.md and
any report text, and the C-1 row is restated as whatever the twenty chains show. The
2026-09-14 result is not deleted; it is marked superseded in gates/retractions.json
the same way 2.94x was.
verdict_if_passed: The protection effect is real at n = 20. Replace the 'roughly nine times' wording with
the measured ratio and its interval, and record the n = 3 figure as superseded rather
than as wrong.
sanity_check: Recomputing the first three chains of the new intact arm must reproduce the 2026-09-14
means of 11.3 and 1.3 if and only if the same seeds are used. They are not, so this is
reported as a comparison rather than enforced as a gate — but a new intact mean far
outside the old per-seed range of 9 to 13 means the harness changed, not the finding.

C-2R.name: No chaining, re-checked against a compute-matched reference
C-2R.question: Does the chain still leave the one-step reference when that reference is given the same total training compute the chain spent?
background: C-2 compared 25-generation chains against one-step students trained for 1500 steps,
which matches the budget of each individual chain student. C-3 then showed that
one-step agreement is an optimization quantity rather than an information limit: it
rises monotonically with training budget, from 0.142 at 375 steps to 0.306 at 12000.
That leaves C-2's escape generations (4, 7 and 16) defined against a reference that
moves, and it leaves one serious objection unanswered. The chain spends 25 x 1500 =
37500 optimizer steps in total. A critic can say the chain does not lose information
at all — it accumulates optimization error, and a single student given the same total
compute would look just as far from the founder. This entry tests exactly that.
The chains are not re-run. The comparison reuses the five chains per condition already
logged in logs/c2_no_chaining.json, so this judges the same chains C-2 judged and only
the reference is new.
C-2R.reference_distribution: one-step students distilled directly from generation 0 and trained for 37500 steps, the chain's entire compute budget spent in a single step

sanity.condition: the 1500-step reference arm reproduces C-2's means, 0.230 within [0.220, 0.243] at B = 4096 and 0.055 within [0.047, 0.064] at B = 128
sanity.meaning_if_failed: the harness is not reproducing C-2 and nothing else in this run can be read

A.metric: agree_gen0 on the held-out probe pool, B = 4096
A.condition: some chain generation g <= 25 falls below the 37500-step reference's 2.5th percentile
A.meaning_if_failed: the chain's functional decay is indistinguishable from one student given the same compute, so 'iteration destroys the function' is not supported and must be restated as accumulated optimization error

B.metric: n_classes_used on the held-out probe pool, B = 128
B.condition: some chain generation g <= 25 falls below the 37500-step reference's 2.5th percentile
B.meaning_if_failed: alphabet contraction is not established against a compute-matched one-step student, and the project's headline result loses its strongest form

derivation: 37500 is not a chosen number. It is 25 generations times the 1500 steps each chain
student trains for, which is the chain's own total compute. Any smaller reference
budget leaves the accumulated-optimization-error objection open; any larger one is
comparing against a student the chain never had the resources to be.
The 2.5th percentile is C-2's own escape criterion, reused unchanged so that the two
controls are directly comparable. 20 students per arm rather than C-2's 50, because a
37500-step student costs 25 times a standard one; 20 is the same n C-3 used for its
budget sweep.
verdict_if_failed: If gate A fails: C-2's function result is restated. The chain is not shown to lose
anything a compute-matched single step does not, and every claim resting on the escape
generations 4 and 16 is withdrawn pending a better design.
If gate B fails: this is the serious one. 'One step destroys the function, repetition
destroys the vocabulary' is the project's sharpest claim and it appears in
progress-report-2.md. If a compute-matched one-step student also collapses its
alphabet, that sentence is wrong and must be retracted in the same session the result
lands.
verdict_if_passed: The escape survives the strongest available form of the C-3 objection. C-2's escape
generations stand, now qualified by the reference budget they were measured against,
and every decay claim can name a compute-matched floor rather than a step-matched one.
sanity_check: Reported alongside the gates, not gated on: the 37500-step reference's mean agreement
should exceed C-3's 12000-step value of 0.306 at B = 4096. If it does not, the extra
budget is not buying fidelity and the compute-matched framing needs rethinking before
the gates are read.

C-4T.name: Matched imbalance, timing test — do starved classes die sooner?
C-4T.question: Does how much transmitted signal a class receives predict how long it survives?
background: C-4 ran on 2026-09-29 and returned a verdict of FAILED on gate A: soft-logit
transmission does starve classes, 26 of them below one effective example at the first
transmission across five chains. That closed the cheap evasion route.
C-4's gate B was supposed to decide whether the starvation matters, and it could not.
It compared the classes starved at generation 1 against the classes absent at
generation 25, and by generation 25 between 37 and 48 of the 50 classes are absent, so
a randomly chosen set of three to seven classes already overlaps the dead set at 0.880.
The observed 0.971 against that null gives p = 0.1004 with 0.12 of headroom. The gate
passed and means nothing. The defect is in the gate, not in the data.
The fault is that an endpoint comparison at generation 25 is saturated. Timing is not.
A class that is starved from the start and dies at generation 3 is a different object
from one that dies at generation 22, and minority collapse predicts the first.
This gate is written before the data it reads exists. logs/c4_class_mass.json records
n_classes_used per generation but never WHICH classes, so per-class death generations
cannot be recovered from it and a re-run is required. The chains are seed-identical, so
the re-run reproduces C-4's mass and starvation numbers exactly; what is new is the
per-generation alphabet membership, which no run in this project has ever recorded.
C-4T.metric: death generation d_k of each class k: the first generation at which class k is absent from the student's predictions on the held-out probe pool and remains absent through generation 25. Classes still predicted at generation 25 are censored at d_k = 26.

A.metric: Spearman rank correlation between a class's effective transmitted count at generation 1 and its death generation, pooled across the five chains
A.condition: the correlation is not significantly positive
A.fails_if: one-sided permutation p < 0.05 for a positive correlation, permuting class labels within each chain, 10000 permutations
A.meaning_if_failed: how much signal a class receives predicts how long it lives, which is what minority collapse asserts; the constructed matched-imbalance control becomes mandatory and the contraction claim must name this explanation as unexcluded

B.metric: difference in mean death generation between the classes starved at generation 1 and all other classes, pooled across the five chains
B.condition: starved classes do not die earlier than the rest
B.fails_if: one-sided permutation p < 0.05 for starved classes dying earlier, same permutation scheme
B.meaning_if_failed: the same conclusion as gate A, restricted to the starved set C-4 already identified

derivation: Gate A uses all fifty classes rather than only the three to seven starved ones. That is
the direct fix for what broke C-4's gate B: the endpoint statistic had five classes and
a saturated null, this one has fifty classes and a response variable spread over
twenty-five generations.
Spearman rather than Pearson because effective transmitted counts are heavily skewed —
C-4 measured minima near 0.02 against a uniform 2.56 — and because death generation is
censored at 26, which makes a rank statistic the honest choice.
The 0.05 level and the permutation scheme are the repository's existing convention,
from analysis/seed_stability_stats.py. Permuting class labels WITHIN each chain, rather
than pooling classes across chains first, keeps each chain's own death-generation
distribution fixed so the test asks only whether the class identities line up.
Direction matters and is fixed here in advance: a POSITIVE correlation means
better-fed classes live longer, which supports minority collapse. That is the outcome
that fails this gate. A null result is what clears the objection, which means this gate
can only ever weaken the project's position or leave it unchanged — it cannot
manufacture support for the headline claim.
verdict_if_failed: Minority collapse is a live explanation for alphabet contraction. The constructed
matched-imbalance control moves from optional to mandatory, and until it runs, every
statement of the contraction result — in README.md, in progress-report-2.md, and in any
report text — must name Fang et al. (2021) as an unexcluded alternative explanation.
verdict_if_passed: How much signal a class receives does not predict how long it survives. Starvation is
present but inert, minority collapse is excluded as the mechanism for this result, and
C-4's gate A failure can be reported as a measured fact with no consequence for the
contraction claim.
sanity_check: The re-run must reproduce C-4's generation-1 starvation counts exactly — 4, 7, 5, 7 and
3 for chain seeds 400 through 404 — since the seeds and configuration are unchanged. If
it does not, the re-run is not the same experiment and the timing numbers cannot be
attached to C-4's result.

C-4F.name: Frequency-matched null for the starved-class timing effect
C-4F.question: Does C-4T's timing effect survive a null that holds the founder's generation-0 class frequency fixed, or does it reduce to the fact that a class the founder itself rarely predicts is marginal everywhere?
background: C-4T ran on 2026-09-29 and failed both gates. The pooled Spearman correlation between a
class's effective transmitted count at generation 1 and its death generation was 0.363 at
p = 1.0e-4, and the classes starved at generation 1 died 5.51 generations earlier than the
rest at p = 1.0e-4, both over 10000 permutations. Minority collapse is therefore recorded
as an unexcluded explanation for alphabet contraction, and commit 914028b names Fang et
al. (2021) as such in the published text.
Both of C-4T's nulls are uniform over classes. Its gate A permuted each chain's death
generations among all fifty classes; its gate B reassigned the starved label uniformly at
fixed set size. Neither null knows anything about the founder. That is the defect this
control addresses. A class the founder itself rarely predicts contributes little softmax
mass to any transmitted set, so it is starved at generation 1 close to by construction,
and it may die early for a reason that has nothing to do with the mechanism Fang et al.
describe: it was already marginal in generation 0. Under a uniform null, 'starved' and
'founder-rare' are not separable, and C-4T cannot say which of the two its correlation
measures.
This is the question progress-report-2.md section 5 ranks first, and the reason it ranks
first governs the schedule: if the timing effect reduces to founder class frequency, then
the constructed matched-imbalance control, which C-4T moved from optional to mandatory, is
aimed at the wrong target and should not be built yet.
Both outcomes of this control cost something, and that is recorded here before the run
rather than discovered after it. If the effect survives frequency matching, minority
collapse stands as a mechanism and the expensive control is owed. If it does not, the
timing effect is a founder-frequency effect, which is the 'frequent classes survive'
explanation RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 4.3 names as the boring rival to the founder-identity
claim. No outcome here leaves the project's position unchanged, and these gates must not
be read as though one did.
No new chains are trained. Death generations, generation-1 transmitted mass and the
generation-1 starved sets are read unmodified from logs/c4_timing.json, which
controls/c4_timing.py produced on this machine. The founder is rebuilt from train_seed 0
to obtain the generation-0 per-class predicted frequency on the held-out probe pool at
probe_seed 9000, which is the covariate the matching needs and which no existing log
records.
C-4F.metric: death generation d_k exactly as C-4T defines it (the first generation at which class k is absent from the student's predictions on the held-out probe pool and remains absent through generation 25; classes still predicted at generation 25 are censored at 26), paired with founder generation-0 predicted class frequency, the number of held-out probe-pool points the founder assigns to class k by argmax

A.metric: difference in mean death generation between the classes starved at generation 1 and all other classes, pooled across the five chains — the same statistic C-4T gate B used, against a different null
A.condition: the starved classes do not die earlier than the rest once the null is matched on founder generation-0 predicted frequency
A.fails_if: one-sided permutation p < 0.05 for starved classes dying earlier, where the null draws fake starved sets of the observed per-chain size carrying the same founder-frequency stratum profile as the real starved set — five strata of ten classes each, formed by ranking the fifty classes on founder generation-0 predicted frequency — over 10000 permutations
A.meaning_if_failed: starvation predicts death timing beyond the founder's own class frequency, so minority collapse is not reducible to the boring explanation and the constructed matched-imbalance control at depth is owed
A.meaning_if_passed: the timing effect is a founder-frequency effect; C-4T's gate B result must be restated as such, and 'frequent classes survive' moves from a rival to the leading account of alphabet contraction, which C-4S then has to measure directly

B.metric: pooled Spearman rank correlation between effective transmitted count at generation 1 and death generation — the same statistic C-4T gate A used, against a different null
B.condition: the correlation is not significantly positive once the null permutes death generations only within founder-frequency strata
B.fails_if: one-sided permutation p < 0.05 for a positive correlation, where the null permutes each chain's death generations within the five founder-frequency strata rather than across all fifty classes, over 10000 permutations
B.meaning_if_failed: the dose-response relation between transmitted signal and survival time is not an artifact of founder frequency, and the same consequence as gate A follows
B.meaning_if_passed: the continuous version of the effect is explained by founder frequency, and C-4T's gate A correlation of 0.363 must be reported as confounded with it

headroom: Reported in the log beside every p-value this control produces: the null mean, the null
standard deviation, and the number of distinct fake assignments the matching leaves
available. A gate is declared NOT EVALUABLE, and no verdict is taken from it, if the null
standard deviation is below 1.0 generation or fewer than 1000 distinct fake starved sets
are achievable.
Derivation of the 1.0-generation floor: death generation is integer-valued on 1 to 26, so
a null that cannot produce a difference of one whole generation cannot resolve a
difference of one whole generation. The floor is the metric's own quantum, not a tuned
constant.
Derivation of the 1000-set floor: stratified matching constrains the draw, and a starved
set that exhausts its strata leaves a null that is nearly deterministic. Two gates in this
project have already passed while incapable of detecting anything. C-4's gate B compared
the starved classes against the classes dead at generation 25, but 37 to 48 of 50 are dead
by then, so a random set of three to seven classes already overlapped the dead set at a
null of 0.880 on a statistic bounded at 1.0, leaving 0.12 of headroom and returning
p = 0.1004. C-2R's gates fired at generation 1, before any chaining existed, and so
compared a short-trained student against a long-trained one and rediscovered C-3. Both
failed the same way: neither asked what its statistic does when the comparison is already
saturated. Writing the rule before the run prevents moving the threshold afterwards; it
does not prevent writing one that cannot see. Every gate from this entry onward reports
what room it had.
combination: How the two gates combine into one verdict, specified here because leaving it to the
script would be a decision made in code rather than committed in advance.
Both gates evaluable: the control PASSES only if both pass, and FAILS if either fails.
Exactly one gate evaluable: the verdict is PARTIAL. It carries that gate's consequence
and no more, and every statement of it must name which gate carried it and which was
refused. Neither gate evaluable: NOT EVALUABLE, and nothing is concluded.
C-4T's script took the stricter line that any unreadable gate makes the whole control
inconclusive. The weaker line is taken here for a stated reason: C-4F's two gates test
the same hypothesis through two statistics - a set contrast and a continuous correlation
- so one readable gate is real evidence about that hypothesis, where C-4T's gate A and
gate B were a correlation and a subgroup comparison that could come apart. PARTIAL is
the label for evidence that is real and incomplete, and it is not to be reported as a
pass or a failure.
derivation: The five-stratum choice is the coarsest partition that still separates the starved sets
from the rest of the alphabet: the starved sets C-4T observed run three to seven classes,
so ten-class strata leave every stratum larger than any starved set and the matching
therefore always has freedom to draw. Finer strata would tighten the match but shrink that
freedom toward the degenerate null the headroom rule above exists to catch, and the
headroom rule, not a preference, is what decides whether five was coarse enough: if the
null standard deviation clears 1.0 generation the stratification was usable, and if it
does not the gate reports NOT EVALUABLE rather than a verdict.
The 0.05 one-sided level and the 10000 permutations are carried over unchanged from C-4
and C-4T so that this control's numbers are comparable to theirs. The direction is fixed
here as it was there: a significant effect is what FAILS the gate. This control cannot
manufacture support for the headline claim, only move which explanation the project owes
an answer to.
verdict_if_failed: C-4T's timing effect is not reducible to founder class frequency. Minority collapse remains
a live mechanism for alphabet contraction, every statement of the contraction result
continues to name Fang et al. (2021) as an unexcluded alternative, and the constructed
matched-imbalance control at depth is now the next experiment owed rather than one option
among several.
verdict_if_passed: The starved classes' early death is a founder-frequency effect. C-4T's two failures must be
restated in README.md and in any report text as confounded with founder generation-0 class
frequency rather than as evidence for minority collapse, and the constructed
matched-imbalance control is deferred until C-4S establishes whether founder frequency
explains survival outright. This is not a clean result for the project: it replaces one
competing explanation with another, and the replacement bears on the founder-identity
claim rather than on the contraction claim.
sanity_check: The founder rebuilt by this control must reproduce the memorization accuracy recorded in
logs/c4_timing.json, 0.977294921875, exactly. If it does not, the frequency covariate does
not belong to the founder whose chains produced those death generations, the matching is
meaningless, and the gates must not be read.
The matched null must reproduce the real starved set's stratum profile exactly on every
draw; this is asserted per draw, not spot-checked.
Recomputing C-4T's two statistics under C-4T's own uniform nulls from the same log must
return its published numbers, 0.363 and -5.51. That establishes that any difference this
control reports comes from the null and not from the data handling.
logs/c4_timing.json is read and never rewritten.

C-4S.name: Per-class survival regression
C-4S.question: What predicts how long a class survives — the signal it receives in transmission, or properties the founder already had before any transmission happened?
background: RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 4.3 calls this analysis 'free, and the analysis most likely to
change the conclusion', and states the stake plainly: if founder class frequency alone
explains survival, the founder-identity story reduces to 'frequent classes survive.'
PROJECT.md's strongest claim is that the founder's identity survives in the code long
after it is gone from the function, and that claim currently rests on survivor-set
overlap, which is consistent with the frequency explanation.
C-4F and this control ask different questions and are preregistered together, before
either runs. C-4F asks whether C-4T's effect is confounded with founder frequency. C-4S
asks what the operative variable actually is, over the full set of predictors section 4.3
names. Neither needs a new chain.
The outcome is death generation rather than a binary survival indicator at generation 25,
because C-4 established that 37 to 48 of the 50 classes are already dead by then. An
endpoint indicator is the saturated comparison that made C-4's gate B unreadable.
Censoring is real but light in rank terms: two to thirteen classes per chain are censored
at 26, which is why both gates below are rank-based rather than least-squares fits, and
why no coefficient from a linear model is used as a gate statistic.
C-4S.metric: death generation d_k as C-4T defines it, related in rank terms to the predictors RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 4.3 names: founder generation-0 predicted frequency on the held-out probe pool; founder generation-0 mean top-1 margin over the probe points it assigns to class k; the L2 norm of the founder head's weight row for class k; the sum of that row; the mean feature norm over probe points the founder assigns to class k; and the effective transmitted count at generation 1. All six are derived from the founder at train_seed 0 or read from logs/c4_timing.json; none requires a new run.

A.metric: pooled Spearman rank correlation between founder generation-0 predicted class frequency and death generation
A.condition: founder generation-0 class frequency does not by itself predict how long a class survives
A.fails_if: one-sided permutation p < 0.05 for a positive correlation, permuting death generations within each chain, over 10000 permutations
A.meaning_if_failed: the classes that survive are the ones the founder already predicted often, so every statement of the founder-identity result must say that founder class frequency is a sufficient predictor of survival, and the surviving-alphabet overlap cannot be attributed to founder identity beyond frequency without a frequency-matched overlap null
A.meaning_if_passed: the boring explanation is excluded on this data and the founder-identity claim survives its cheapest available challenge

B.metric: pooled Spearman rank correlation between the L2 norm of the founder head's weight row for class k and death generation, after both have been residualised on founder generation-0 predicted frequency by rank regression
B.condition: the founder's head geometry carries no information about survival time beyond what its predicted class frequency already carries
B.fails_if: two-sided permutation p < 0.05 for the partial correlation, permuting the residualised head norms within each chain, over 10000 permutations
B.meaning_if_failed: survival time is predicted by the founder's readout geometry and not only by its output distribution, which is a representation-level result and is reported as one; it does not rescue the founder-identity claim from gate A and must not be presented as though it did
B.meaning_if_passed: the founder-side account of survival is purely a frequency account, which simplifies the story and narrows what the sampler arm has to explain

headroom: Reported in the log beside every p-value this control produces: the null mean, the null
standard deviation, and the rank variance of each residual the gate depends on. A gate is
declared NOT EVALUABLE, and no verdict is taken from it, if the null standard deviation is
below the resolution of the statistic it tests.
For this control the relevant degeneracy differs from C-4F's and is checked directly: a
partial correlation is undefined when the residual of either variable has zero variance,
and it is uninterpretable when founder frequency already explains almost all of the rank
variance in the other predictor. Gate B therefore reports the rank variance of both
residuals and is declared NOT EVALUABLE if either falls below one percent of the
unresidualised rank variance, since a partial correlation computed on nothing is the error
C-4's gate B made in a different coordinate system.
combination: Both gates evaluable: the control PASSES only if both pass, and FAILS if either fails.
Exactly one gate evaluable: the verdict is PARTIAL, carrying that gate's consequence and
no more, and naming which gate carried it. Neither evaluable: NOT EVALUABLE.
The two gates here are less interchangeable than C-4F's, since gate A tests the boring
explanation and gate B tests a representation-level predictor, so a PARTIAL verdict must
state which of those two questions was answered and leave the other open rather than
implying both.
derivation: Gate A is one-sided because the boring explanation makes a signed prediction: classes the
founder predicts more often should survive longer, not merely differently. Gate B is
two-sided because no theory in this project predicts the sign of a head-norm effect, and
committing to a direction there would be a guess dressed as a hypothesis.
The 0.05 level, the 10000 permutations and the within-chain permutation scheme are carried
over from C-4T unchanged, for comparability. Only two of the six predictors carry gates.
The other four — top-1 margin, head row sum, mean feature norm, and generation-1
transmitted count — are reported with their correlations and bootstrap intervals as
descriptives. This is deliberate: six gates at 0.05 would be a multiple-comparisons
problem, and the two that carry decisions are the two whose outcomes change what the
report claims.
verdict_if_failed: Survival time is predicted by properties the founder had before any transmission. The
founder-identity claim in PROJECT.md must be restated to say what it adds over founder
class frequency, and the frequency-matched overlap null in RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 4.3
item 3 becomes a prerequisite for any further statement about founder identity rather than
an improvement to the statistics.
verdict_if_passed: Neither founder class frequency nor founder head geometry predicts survival time on this
data. The founder-identity claim survives, the surviving alphabet is not merely the
founder's frequent classes, and the descriptive correlations for the remaining four
predictors are reported as the measured context for that.
sanity_check: The founder rebuilt here must reproduce the memorization accuracy recorded in
logs/c4_timing.json, 0.977294921875, exactly, for the same reason C-4F requires it.
Founder generation-0 predicted frequencies must sum to the probe-pool size, 4096.
Death generations are read from logs/c4_timing.json and must reproduce the per-chain mean
death generations that log already records. logs/c4_timing.json is read and never
rewritten.

C-4O.name: Frequency-matched null for the same-founder survivor-set overlap
C-4O.question: Does the same-founder survivor-set overlap survive a null that draws survivors in proportion to the founder's own generation-0 class frequency, or does 'founder identity' reduce to 'founder class-frequency imbalance'?
background: C-4S ran on 2026-10-20 and failed both gates. Founder generation-0 predicted class
frequency alone correlates with death generation at 0.4721 over 10000 within-chain
permutations, p = 1.0e-4, which is a larger correlation than the 0.3625 transmitted-count
effect C-4T rests on. Frequent classes survive longer, and two chains descending from one
founder inherit the same class frequencies.
That makes the project's strongest claim unsafe as stated. Arm A of the n = 20
seed-stability run gives a mean pairwise Jaccard of 0.193 among the survivor sets of
twenty chains from one shared founder, against an empirical null of 0.091 - the 2.12x
figure - with a 95% interval of [0.152, 0.236] and a cross-arm permutation p = 1.0e-4.
Every one of those numbers is measured against a null that draws survivors uniformly over
the fifty classes. A uniform null knows nothing about the founder, so under it
'same founder' and 'same output frequencies' are not separable, exactly as C-4T's uniform
nulls could not separate 'starved' from 'founder-rare'. This is the same defect in a
second place, and it was found by a control rather than by rereading the claim.
C-4S's committed consequence names this control as a prerequisite for any further
statement about founder identity rather than as an improvement to the statistics, and
README.md and PROJECT.md were qualified on 2026-10-20 to say the overlap must not be
presented as evidence of founder identity until it has run. This entry is what lifts or
confirms that qualification.
Both outcomes cost something and that is recorded here before the run. If the overlap
survives frequency matching, founder identity adds something beyond the founder's output
distribution, the qualification is lifted, and the 2.12x result is stronger than it was
before C-4S because it has now survived the challenge C-4S raised. If it does not, the
founder-identity claim is withdrawn as such and restated as a class-frequency claim,
which is the 'frequent classes survive' account RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 4.3 names as the
boring rival, and PROJECT.md's strongest claim goes with it.
No chains are trained. Arm A's twenty survivor sets are read unmodified from
logs/seed_stability_n20.json. The founder is rebuilt from founder_seed 0 at 3000 steps,
which run_seed_stability.py's Arm A founder and controls/c4_timing.py's founder both are,
verified by the memorization accuracy 0.977294921875 that both logs record.
The weights are measured on the TRAINING pool, make_pool(seed=0, kind='noise'), and not
on the held-out probe pool C-4F and C-4S used. This is deliberate and is the one place
this control could have repeated a defect the project has already paid for:
run_seed_stability.py computes each chain's survivor set as the classes the final teacher
predicts on that training pool, so a probe-pool frequency vector would be a weighting from
one pool applied to sets defined on another - the same splice withdrawn from
figs/fig2_cka_blindness.png on 2026-10-20. Each control's covariate is measured on the
pool its outcome is defined on, and the two controls differ for that reason and not by
oversight.
C-4O.metric: mean pairwise set overlap among Arm A's twenty survivor sets - 190 pairs - computed by analysis/overlap_stats.py, against a null drawn by draw_survivors_weighted at the observed per-run set sizes with class draw probability proportional to the founder's generation-0 predicted class frequency on the training pool
sampler_limitation: draw_survivors_weighted draws without replacement with renormalization, so the first
class in a set is drawn with probability exactly proportional to the weights but the
per-class inclusion probability for a set of size k > 1 is not. Its own docstring states
this and states that no without-replacement scheme can make inclusion exactly
proportional while drawing exactly k distinct classes. What the null preserves is the
ordering: heavier classes are included more often.
This bounds the conclusion and the bound is written here rather than discovered in a
review. A verdict from this control is a statement about an ordering-matched frequency
null, not an exactly frequency-matched one. If the overlap survives, the correct claim is
that it is not explained by the founder's class-frequency ordering. A control needing
exact inclusion probabilities needs a different sampler and is not this one.

A.metric: mean pairwise Jaccard over Arm A's twenty survivor sets, the statistic the published 2.12x figure is computed from
A.condition: the observed same-founder overlap is not above a frequency-matched null
A.fails_if: one-sided resampling p < 0.05 for the observed mean pairwise Jaccard exceeding the frequency-matched null, over 10000 draws
A.meaning_if_failed: the same-founder overlap is not explained by the founder's class-frequency ordering, so founder identity adds something beyond the founder's output distribution; the qualification added to README.md and PROJECT.md on 2026-10-20 is lifted and the 2.12x result is reported as having survived C-4S's challenge
A.meaning_if_passed: the same-founder overlap is within what the founder's class-frequency ordering alone produces; the founder-identity claim is withdrawn as such, restated as a class-frequency claim, and PROJECT.md's strongest claim is withdrawn with it

B.metric: mean pairwise overlap coefficient over the same twenty survivor sets, against the same frequency-matched null
B.condition: the observed same-founder overlap is not above a frequency-matched null when measured by a size-insensitive statistic
B.fails_if: one-sided resampling p < 0.05 for the observed mean pairwise overlap coefficient exceeding the frequency-matched null, over 10000 draws
B.meaning_if_failed: the same consequence as gate A, and additionally that the result does not depend on Jaccard's sensitivity to set size, which RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 4.3 item 4 raises as a defect because survivor-set sizes differ systematically across arms
B.meaning_if_passed: the overlap is within the frequency-matched null on the size-insensitive statistic; if gate A fails while this one passes, the gate A result is attributable to set-size differences rather than to shared class membership and must be reported as such

headroom: Reported in the log beside every p-value: the observed statistic, the frequency-matched
null's mean, standard deviation and range, the size-conditioned uniform null's mean for
comparison, and the number of distinct survivor-set assignments the weighting leaves
available. null_headroom is called on every null and its output is logged.
A gate is declared NOT EVALUABLE, and no verdict is taken from it, if any of three floors
is breached.
1. Null standard deviation below 0.004. Derivation: the observed statistic's own 95%
interval is [0.152, 0.236], a half-width of 0.042, which is the spread the data itself
exhibits across chains. A null narrower than a tenth of that cannot represent the
sampling variability the measurement already shows, and a p-value from it would be a
statement about a point mass. The floor is read off the data's own interval, not chosen.
2. Fewer than 1000 distinct survivor-set assignments achievable under the weighting.
Carried over from C-4F unchanged. A weighting concentrated on a handful of classes leaves
a null that is nearly deterministic, which is C-4's gate B failure in another coordinate
system.
3. The frequency-matched null's mean within one of its own standard deviations of the
size-conditioned uniform null's mean. This floor is specific to this control and is the
one most likely to fire. If weighting by founder frequency does not move the null, then
this control is the uniform null wearing a different name, and a verdict from it would be
reported as a test of frequency matching while testing nothing of the kind. The founder's
frequencies are known to be non-uniform - its fifty classes fall into five strata holding
444, 674, 828, 977 and 1173 of the 4096 probe points, a 2.6x spread from rarest decile to
commonest - but that is measured on the probe pool and this control weights on the
training pool, so the separation is checked and not assumed.
combination: Both gates evaluable: the control PASSES only if both pass, and FAILS if either fails.
Exactly one gate evaluable: the verdict is PARTIAL, carrying that gate's consequence and
no more, and naming which gate carried it. Neither evaluable: NOT EVALUABLE, and the
qualification on README.md and PROJECT.md stays in place, because a control that could
not be read removes nothing.
The asymmetry in gate B's meaning_if_passed is deliberate: gate A failing while gate B
passes is not a partial success but a specific finding about set size, and must be
reported as that rather than as a weaker version of gate A.
sanity_check: The founder rebuilt here must reproduce the memorization accuracy both
logs/seed_stability_n20.json and logs/c4_timing.json record, 0.977294921875, exactly.
Arm A must carry twenty runs at founder_seed 0 and chain seeds 100 to 119; a log with
different seeds is not the run whose null this control replaces.
The observed mean pairwise Jaccard recomputed here must reproduce the 0.193 that
analysis/seed_stability_stats.py reports from the same log, and the size-conditioned
uniform null mean must reproduce its 0.091, to three decimal places. If the statistic
cannot be reproduced, the frequency-matched null is being compared against a different
quantity than the published figure and no verdict is taken.
logs/seed_stability_n20.json is read and never rewritten.
verdict_if_failed: The same-founder survivor-set overlap is not explained by the founder's class-frequency
ordering. Founder identity adds something beyond the founder's output distribution, the
2026-10-20 qualification on README.md and PROJECT.md is lifted, and the claim is restated
as having survived the challenge C-4S raised rather than as never having faced it.
C-4S's gate A result stands unchanged: founder frequency still predicts survival time, it
just does not account for where a chain ends up.
verdict_if_passed: The same-founder overlap is within what the founder's class-frequency ordering alone
produces. The founder-identity claim is withdrawn as such and restated as a class-frequency
claim; PROJECT.md's strongest claim, that the founder's identity survives in the code long
after it is gone from the function, is withdrawn with it. The surviving statement is that
chains from one founder inherit its class frequencies and that frequent classes survive,
which is C-4S's gate A result and is already established. The seed-stability experiment
then measures a consequence of frequency rather than a founder effect, and the
cross-arm permutation result must be reread in that light.

S-1.name: The learner-rule arm: posterior-sampled weights at temperature lambda
S-1.question: Does replacing the maximizer learner with a posterior sampler change where a chain ends up - and if it does not, was the sampler actually a sampler?
background: RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 4.2 calls this arm the spine of the semester and section 7
requires six things committed to a timestamped file before the week-9 dose-response sweep
runs. Ten controls are preregistered in this file and none of them is this arm. That is the
gap this entry closes, and it closes it before any sampler code exists, not after.
Section 7's last item is the one that matters: the rule distinguishing 'the
sampler/maximizer distinction does not transfer' from 'the sampler was not a sampler'. The
plan says writing it after seeing the result is worthless. A null result from an inert
sampler is indistinguishable from a null result from a working one unless the inertness
threshold is fixed first, so the inertness check below is a PRECONDITION and not a gate: if
it fails, no gate here is read at all and the arm is reported BROKEN rather than null.
Design, from section 4.2. The target is p(w | D) proportional to p(D | w)^lambda times
p(w). Large lambda is the existing maximizer arm and lambda = 1 is honest Bayes, so one
scalar connects the published Arm B continuously to this arm and turns a yes/no into a
dose-response curve. Two prerequisites the plan flags as easy to miss, both verified in the
code on 2026-10-20. First, there is currently no prior for a chain to converge to: every
train() call passes wd = 0.0 into AdamW's weight_decay (spike_iterated_distill.py:100), an
improper flat prior over the model's 91698 parameters, so 'converges to the learner's prior'
is undefined as the code stands. Second, KL-to-soft-logits is not a log-likelihood, so the
arm is built on top of sampler_arm.py's sampled hard labels, which give an honest
categorical likelihood with N = B observations. Griffiths and Kalish require two sampling
steps; sampler_arm.py already implements the production step correctly and lacks the
learning step. This arm is the learning step.
Method, from the section 4.2 ranking table. Primary is anchored / randomized-MAP at K = 1,
listed at 1.0x the cost of SGD and about 5 lines. The negative control is MC dropout,
listed at 1.0x and about 3 lines and marked in that table as NOT a genuine posterior
sampler - a fixed mask distribution around one point. Cost is therefore not what has been
blocking this arm, and that should be said plainly: what blocked it was that its decision
rules were unwritten.
Correctness, not just significance. Section 4.1's C-8 freezes model.body and trains only
the head, which makes the head a GLM whose Laplace posterior is closed form, and the plan
states that the analytic prediction and the experiment must then agree - 'a correctness
check on the sampler implementation that nothing else in the design provides'. C-8 is
therefore a prerequisite of this arm and not a side control, and it is listed as such in
the order of work below rather than left to be discovered.

fixed_in_advance.lambda_infinity_reference: the existing maximizer arm, which is lambda -> infinity by construction and is not rerun
fixed_in_advance.sigma_grid: two values per layer: sigma_match, set per-layer to that layer's measured initialization standard deviation, and 4 x sigma_match
fixed_in_advance.transmission: sampled hard labels, as sampler_arm.py already implements
fixed_in_advance.negative_control: MC dropout, same budget, same grid
fixed_in_advance.secondary_statistic: cross-arm permutation test on mean pairwise Jaccard of survivor sets
fixed_in_advance.multiplicity_correction: Holm-Bonferroni across gates A, B and C, fixed here before any run

sigma_derivation: sigma is not a nuisance parameter - section 4.2 states it defines the attractor the theory
predicts - so its grid cannot be chosen after seeing a result. Both values are read off the
code rather than picked. sigma_match is each layer's own initialization standard deviation,
measured on 2026-10-20 from MLP at torch.manual_seed(0): 0.0817 for body.0, 0.0360 for
body.2, 0.0361 for head, consistent with PyTorch's default kaiming_uniform bound of
1/sqrt(fan_in) at fan_in 50, 256 and 256. A prior at that scale is the one the maximizer
arm already behaves as though it had. The second value is 4x, because that is the smallest
multiple that places the prior's mass outside the bulk of the initialization distribution,
which is what the falsification test in gate C needs in order to produce two genuinely
different attractors rather than two labels for one.
precondition_sampler_exactness: ADDED 2026-10-23, three days after this entry was committed on 2026-10-20, and that date is
part of what is committed here. Nothing in this arm has been built or run, so no result
existed to tighten a rule around; what prompted it was finding that RESEARCH-PLAN.md's
sampler formula was wrong, not finding an outcome that needed excluding. This entry's
primary method was and remains 'anchored / randomized-MAP at K = 1', which IS
randomize-then-optimize, so the committed rule was never wrong - only the plan's prose and
formula were, and those were corrected the same day. This is therefore an addition to S-1
and not a retraction of it.
Read FIRST, before the inertness precondition and before any gate. The sampler's own stated
exactness condition is tested directly: with a linear forward model, Gaussian noise and a
Gaussian prior, randomize-then-optimize draws are exact posterior samples (Bardsley,
Solonen, Haario and Laine 2014, DOI 10.1137/140964023, whose abstract states that in the
linear case the samples are directly from the posterior density). That condition is
checkable in seconds against a closed-form posterior, with no frozen body, no GLM and no
chain, by analysis/anchored_sampler_check.py.
The check. The arm's weight-draw step is exercised on a linear-Gaussian problem at N = 60,
D = 8, noise sd 0.5, prior sd 1.3, 20000 draws, on at least three seeds, and compared to the
closed-form posterior on three quantities. The posterior mean: the worst coordinate's
deviation must be within 5 standard errors of the exact marginal standard deviation. Every
marginal standard deviation: the ratio to the exact posterior must be within 1 +/- 0.05 in
EVERY coordinate, not on average. The total variance: the trace ratio must be within
1 +/- 0.05. All three must hold on every seed.
The arm is declared BROKEN, the inertness precondition is not read, NO gate below is read,
and no statement is made about whether the sampler/maximizer distinction transfers, unless
all three hold on every seed.
Why this is ahead of inertness rather than beside it. The anchor-only variant of the same
method - draw the anchor, leave the transmitted targets alone - would pass every other check
in this entry. It passes inertness, because its draws genuinely do differ. It is not MC
dropout, so the negative control stays clean. It is correctly centred with the prior
entering through the anchor, so it would plausibly still produce sigma-dependent attractors
and satisfy gate C. Measured on 2026-10-23 at the shape above, it is 12.3x to 22.3x too
narrow, with a trace ratio of 0.003 to 0.005, while sitting within 0.07 standard errors of
the posterior mean (logs/anchored_sampler_exactness.txt, seeds 0, 1 and 2). Stated
generally: inertness, the MC-dropout control and gate C all detect whether the draws DIFFER,
and none of them detects whether they differ by the RIGHT AMOUNT. A sampler that narrow
reaches a verdict intact, and its null reads as 'the sampler/maximizer distinction does not
transfer' when the truth is 'the sampler was not a sampler' - verbatim the distinction
RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 7 requires be fixed in advance and calls worthless to write
afterwards.
Derivation of the three constants, so that none of them is a number chosen to fit. The 5
percent band on the standard deviations and on the trace is set by Monte-Carlo noise, not by
taste: the relative standard error of an estimated standard deviation is 1/sqrt(2 * draws),
which is 0.5 percent at 20000 draws, so 5 percent is ten Monte-Carlo standard errors from a
correct sampler and cannot fire by chance, while being twenty times looser than the failure
it exists to catch. The 5 standard errors on the mean is multiplicity across the D
coordinates: a two-sided five-sigma coordinate-wise bound has a family-wise false-alarm rate
below 1e-5 at D = 8. The denominator is the EXACT posterior's standard deviation rather than
the sampler's own, which is deliberately generous to a narrow sampler, because a narrow
sampler SHOULD pass the centring test - being correctly centred is exactly what makes it
dangerous. Three seeds rather than one because the ratios are functions of the particular
design matrix.
Two limits, stated here rather than discovered later. First, the check tests the estimator
and not the arm unless the arm's draw step is the code being called: the sampler must be
implemented so that the same function producing a weight draw in the chain can be invoked on
the linear-Gaussian problem. If it cannot be, this check is evidence about
analysis/anchored_sampler_check.py and not about the arm, and must be reported as such.
Second, passing is necessary and not sufficient. An incompletely converged inner
optimization, a weight decay that does not match the sigma in force, or a per-layer sigma
mismatch are all invisible to it. C-8 remains the correctness check on the real model and
this does not replace it; this one catches the error C-8 would not, because C-8 compares a
posterior MEAN and the defect here is entirely in the spread.
A BROKEN verdict is reported as BROKEN. It is not reported as a null result.
precondition_inertness: Read BEFORE any gate and reported whether or not any gate is read. Two students are drawn
from the same posterior on the same transmitted data, differing only in the sampler's
randomness, and their functional disagreement is measured on the held-out probe pool at
probe_seed 9000. The same quantity is measured for the maximizer arm across two training
The arm is declared BROKEN, and NO gate below is read, unless the sampler's draw-to-draw
disagreement exceeds the maximizer's seed-to-seed disagreement with non-overlapping 95
percent intervals at n = 20 per side.
Derivation, and why it is a comparison rather than a constant. Izmailov et al. is the
reason this check exists: an approximate sampler can collapse to a point and still run
without error. A fixed numeric threshold would be a constant chosen by me, and this project
has already shipped two gates whose constants could not see. The maximizer's own seed noise
is the only principled floor available, because it is what the sampler must beat to be
doing anything at all, and it is measured the same way on the same pool. Non-overlapping
intervals rather than a ratio, because a ratio would need its own cutoff.
A BROKEN verdict is reported as BROKEN. It is not reported as a null result, and it does
not license any statement about whether the sampler/maximizer distinction transfers.

A.metric: founder-identification balanced accuracy, leave-one-chain-out: given a chain's generation-25 survivor set, predict which of the 20 founders it descended from, averaged per class so that unequal survivor-set sizes cannot inflate it
A.condition: a chain's endpoint carries no more information about its founder under the sampler than chance
A.fails_if: one-sided permutation p < 0.05 after Holm-Bonferroni, where the null permutes founder labels across chains over 10000 permutations
A.meaning_if_failed: the founder is still recoverable from the endpoint under a posterior sampler, so sampling does not erase founder dependence and the Griffiths-Kalish prediction does not hold in this setting at this lambda
A.meaning_if_passed: the founder is not recoverable under the sampler; combined with a passing inertness precondition this is the positive result the semester is for, and combined with gate C it says the chain converged to the prior rather than to its founder

B.metric: cross-arm permutation test on mean pairwise Jaccard of survivor sets, same-founder arm against different-founder arm, computed by analysis/overlap_stats.py
B.condition: same-founder and different-founder overlap are indistinguishable under the sampler
B.fails_if: one-sided permutation p < 0.05 after Holm-Bonferroni on the arm label over 10000 permutations
B.meaning_if_failed: founder dependence survives in the survivor sets as well as in the identification statistic, which is the same conclusion as gate A reached by a second route
B.meaning_if_passed: the contrast that gives 2.12x in the maximizer arm is absent under the sampler, which is the dose-response result section 4.2 predicts

C.metric: within-sigma cross-founder mean pairwise Jaccard minus across-sigma cross-founder mean pairwise Jaccard
C.condition: the prior scale does not define an attractor: chains at the same sigma are no more alike than chains at different sigma
C.fails_if: one-sided permutation p < 0.05 after Holm-Bonferroni for within-sigma exceeding across-sigma, permuting the sigma label over 10000 permutations
C.meaning_if_failed: two prior scales produce two different attractors, which is the free falsification test section 4.2 names and is positive evidence that the sampler is converging to a prior rather than wandering
C.meaning_if_passed: sigma does not define an attractor on this data. This is the outcome that most threatens the arm's interpretation even if gates A and B pass, because 'the chain forgot its founder' and 'the chain converged to the prior' are then not the same statement, and only the first would be supported

negative_control_requirement: MC dropout is run on the identical grid at identical budget. The section 4.2 table marks
it as not a genuine posterior sampler - a fixed mask distribution around one point - so it
must NOT reproduce whatever gates A, B and C find.
If MC dropout reproduces the arm's result, the result is attributable to injected noise
rather than to posterior sampling, and every verdict above is withdrawn regardless of its
p-value. This is a disconfirmation requirement and carries no p-value of its own; it is
reported as reproduced or not reproduced, with the same statistics and intervals.
MC dropout is also expected to PASS the inertness precondition, because injected mask noise
produces functionally different draws without sampling any posterior. That is precisely why
inertness cannot be the only check, and it is recorded here so that a passing inertness
check is never read as evidence that the sampler is genuine.
headroom: Reported beside every p-value: the null's mean, standard deviation and range, and for every
statistic its chance level and its attainable bound. Three floors, each declaring a gate NOT
EVALUABLE rather than passed.
1. Degenerate alphabet. Founder identification cannot move if every chain collapses to the
same handful of classes. Gate A is NOT EVALUABLE if the mean surviving alphabet at
generation 25 is below 4.0 classes. Derivation: the maximizer arm at this bottleneck
measures 4.4 surviving classes, so 4.0 is just below the regime the comparison arm actually
occupies; beneath it the number of distinct attainable survivor sets is too small for a
20-way identification to be informative, whatever its p-value.
2. Chance-level separation. Balanced accuracy over 20 founders has a chance level of 0.05.
Gate A is NOT EVALUABLE if the permutation null's mean differs from 0.05 by more than one
of its own standard deviations, because a null that does not sit at the statistic's own
chance level is measuring something other than the label permutation it claims to.
3. Null scaling regime, new on 2026-10-20 and the direct consequence of C-4O. The mean
pairwise Jaccard is a U-statistic of order two, so its null standard deviation scales as
1/sqrt(n) when the first-order projection has positive variance and as 1/n when it does
not. A uniform-over-classes null is degenerate in exactly that sense under
class-exchangeability at fixed set sizes, so comparing a non-degenerate null against a
degenerate one compares two different scaling regimes. Gate B and gate C must therefore
report, for each null they use, the number of sets n and an estimate of that first-order
variance, and are NOT EVALUABLE if the two nulls being compared fall in different regimes.
C-4O's separation floor was blind to this and its refusal is not evidence either way about
the present entry.
combination: The exactness precondition is read first, then the inertness precondition. If either fails,
the arm is BROKEN, no gate is read,
and no statement is made about whether the sampler/maximizer distinction transfers.
If the precondition holds, gates A, B and C are read under Holm-Bonferroni. All three
evaluable: the arm PASSES only if all three pass and FAILS if any fails. Some evaluable:
PARTIAL, naming which gates were readable and carrying only their consequences. None
evaluable: NOT EVALUABLE.
Gate C is not interchangeable with A and B, and a PARTIAL verdict must say so. A and B ask
whether the founder is forgotten; C asks whether the prior is found. Passing A and B while
C passes too means the chain forgot its founder without converging to the prior, which is
not the theory's prediction and must not be reported as though it were.
If MC dropout reproduces the finding, every verdict is withdrawn regardless of the above.
order_of_work: 0. The linear-Gaussian exactness check, which costs seconds and needs no model, so there is
no order in which it is more convenient to run it later. ADDED 2026-10-23 with
precondition_sampler_exactness. It is numbered 0 rather than renumbering the four steps
below, so that the committed order is still legible as what it was.
1. C-8, the frozen-body null, which makes the head a GLM with a closed-form Laplace
posterior and is the only correctness check on the sampler implementation the design
provides. Build and run it before trusting any number from this arm.
2. The inertness precondition, including the maximizer seed-noise baseline it compares
3. The MC-dropout negative control, before the real arm rather than after, so that it
cannot be tuned once the arm's result is known.
This order is fixed here because each step can invalidate the next, and running them in
the convenient order is how a result arrives with nothing able to challenge it.
sanity_check: A proper prior must actually be in force: the weight decay passed to train() must be
non-zero in every sampler run and its value recorded, since wd = 0.0 is the improper flat
prior that makes the arm's central claim undefined.
The transmitted labels must be sampled hard labels and not soft logits, because the
likelihood the sampler needs does not exist otherwise.
At lambda = 100 the arm must approximately reproduce the maximizer arm's published
survivor-alphabet behaviour at the same bottleneck. If a large lambda does not look like
the existing arm, the lambda parameterisation is not doing what it claims and no
dose-response reading is taken.
Founder accuracy must be recorded per founder, and any founder whose memorization accuracy
departs from the established 0.977294921875 by more than 0.01 is reported rather than
silently pooled.
verdict_if_failed: Founder dependence survives posterior sampling at the tested lambda values. The
Griffiths-Kalish prediction that a sampling learner converges to the prior does not transfer
to this architecture on this data, and that is the semester's headline result: a measured
negative against a theoretical prediction, scoped to one architecture and one data
distribution. It must be stated with the inertness margin beside it, because the whole
weight of a negative result here rests on the sampler having been real.
verdict_if_passed: The founder is not recoverable from the endpoint under a posterior sampler, while it is
under a maximizer. This is the dose-response result section 4.2 predicts, and it is the
project's only positive finding if it holds. Three things must be reported with it and not
after it: the inertness margin, the MC-dropout comparison, and gate C's verdict, since
without C the claim is 'the founder was forgotten' and not 'the prior was found'.

categorical_sampler_amendment.added: 2026-10-27, before any S-1 sampler code exists. An addition that fixes the categorical draw objective the entry left unstated; it changes no gate, threshold, grid or order.
why: precondition_sampler_exactness certifies randomize-then-optimize, which is exact only for a Gaussian
likelihood. This arm transmits sampled hard labels, a categorical likelihood, and neither this entry
nor RESEARCH-PLAN.md said what 'perturb the targets' means for a class label. Writing the draw
objective after seeing a result would be the forking path section 7 forbids, so it is fixed here.
method: Per generation, two passes on the transmitted batch (x_i, y_i), i = 1..B, B = 128.
(1) MAP pass: minimise lambda * sum_i CE(f(x_i; w), y_i) + sum_l ||w_l||^2 / (2 sigma_l^2), full batch,
sum reduction, optimizer weight_decay = 0. Record f_hat_i and p_hat_i = softmax(f_hat_i).
(2) Draw pass: draw theta0_l ~ N(0, sigma_l^2 I) for every parameter tensor and xi_i ~ N(0, I_K);
lambda * sum_i [ 1/2 (f_i - f_hat_i)^T B_i (f_i - f_hat_i) + (p_hat_i - y_i)^T (f_i - f_hat_i) ]
- sqrt(lambda) * sum_i xi_i^T B_i^{1/2} f_i + sum_l ||w_l - theta0_l||^2 / (2 sigma_l^2),
with B_i = diag(p_hat_i) - p_hat_i p_hat_i^T. The network stays nonlinear; only the likelihood is
replaced by its generalized Gauss-Newton (GGN) quadratic in logit space around the MAP. The trained
student is the weight draw and is the next generation's teacher.
Bias parameters take the prior sd of their own layer's weights. sigma_match lists weights only, so
this closes a gap rather than choosing a value.
In the Gaussian case, B_i = I / s^2, the draw objective is algebraically randomize-then-optimize
with targets y + s * xi / sqrt(lambda), so the SAME draw function must be the one run through
Excluded: cross-entropy against perturbed soft targets onehot + B^{1/2} xi / sqrt(lambda). It is
unbounded below for a ReLU network and diverged at every lambda at 4 x sigma_match in a scratch
citations_verified_2026_10_27: Antoran, Padhy, Barbano, Nalisnick, Janz & Hernandez-Lobato, 'Sampling-based inference for large linear
models, with application to linearised Laplace', arXiv:2210.04994 (ICLR 2023 per the arXiv comment,
proceedings not checked): sample-then-optimise is exact for the conjugate Gaussian linear model, with
B_i evaluated at the network's predictions f(w_bar, x_i).
Immer, Korzepa & Bauer, arXiv:2008.08400 (AISTATS 2021 per the arXiv comment): the GGN approximation is
a local linearization of the network that turns it into a generalized linear model.
Bardsley, Solonen, Haario & Laine 2014, DOI 10.1137/140964023, already cited above.
Not cited, unverified: Matthews, Hron, Turner & Ghahramani 2017 (no resolvable identifier found).
what_the_linear_gaussian_precondition_ce: Anchor scaling, lambda placement, the per-layer prior form, sum reduction and inner-optimiser
convergence on a convex problem. It does NOT certify the B^{1/2} computation, softmax curvature,
MAP convergence, or anything about the nonlinear network. That is why the next precondition exists.
precondition_categorical_ggn_exactness: Read after precondition_sampler_exactness and before inertness. On C-8's frozen body for pool seed 0
(features augmented with a constant column), with C-8's generation-1 hard-label transmitted batch
and sigma = 0.0361, at each lambda in {1, 10, 100}, the same draw function restricted to the head
must reproduce the closed-form tempered GGN-Laplace posterior given by
analysis/laplace_glm.fit_laplace with prior precision alpha / lambda, covariance H^-1 / lambda.
Compared along 200 fixed directions (100 random unit vectors, 100 leading Hessian eigenvectors)
using 2000 draws: every directional variance ratio within 1 +/- 0.10 and the mean within 5 standard
errors in every direction. Derivation: the relative standard error of a variance estimate at 2000
draws is sqrt(2/2000), about 3.2 percent, so 0.10 is about three standard errors; the 5 standard
errors on the mean carries over from precondition_sampler_exactness. Any failure: BROKEN, no gate is
read, and no statement is made about whether the sampler/maximizer distinction transfers.
does_not_certify: Exactness for the full network. The full-network draw targets a MAP-centred GGN-Laplace posterior in
logit space, not p(D|w)^lambda p(w). Every verdict from this arm is stated as holding 'under a
MAP-centred GGN posterior sampler', and is reported beside the MAP-to-MAP spread across MAP seeds,
the draw-to-draw spread at a fixed MAP, and draw versus MAP logit norm.
forecast_recorded_before_the_run: A single-batch scratch probe on 2026-10-27 (one founder, one batch; not in logs/, unverified) found
that at sigma_match with lambda 1 or 10 the MAP is near-uniform over 50 classes (mean max-probability
0.020 to 0.021), and that at lambda = 100 draw-versus-MAP argmax agreement was 0.086. If that holds,
headroom floor 1 will refuse gate A at sigma_match and the lambda = 100 sanity check may fail there.
The sigma grid is NOT changed in response: it was fixed by derivation, and moving it after a probe is
the threshold move this file exists to prevent. The forecast is written here so that a refusal at
sigma_match is read as the predicted consequence of a strong prior, not as a surprise.
