gate_b_arm_assembly.added: 2026-11-08, before any gate B code exists and before any chain has been run. Found while implementing the aggregator, not while reading a result.
the_silence: Gate B's metric reads 'cross-arm permutation test on mean pairwise Jaccard of survivor
sets, same-founder arm against different-founder arm, computed by analysis/overlap_stats.py'.
That module's cross_arm_permutation_test(sets_a, sets_b, ...) takes two LISTS OF SETS and
permutes which set belongs to which list. But same-founder versus different-founder is a
property of a PAIR, not of a set: with 20 founders at R = 2 there are 40 survivor sets, and
every one of them sits in one same-founder pair and 38 different-founder pairs at once. No
partition of the 40 sets into two lists separates the two kinds of pair. The named function
therefore cannot compute the named statistic, and the entry does not say what to do instead.

decision.statistic: mean Jaccard over the 20 same-founder pairs minus mean Jaccard over the 760 different-founder pairs, both taken over the same 40 survivor sets at R = 2.
decision.null: Permute the FOUNDER LABEL across chains, 10000 permutations, holding the survivor sets fixed. Which pairs count as same-founder follows from the permuted labels.
decision.tail: One-sided for same-founder overlap EXCEEDING different-founder overlap, then Holm-Bonferroni across gates A, B and C as already committed.
decision.p_value: The conservative permutation estimate (1 + #{null >= observed}) / (1 + n_perm), matching gate A and analysis/overlap_stats.py.

why_this_assembly_and_not_the_others: Permuting the founder label is the only permutation that is simultaneously a permutation of
'the arm label' in the sense the entry names AND one the pair structure admits: reassigning
founders reassigns which pairs are same-founder, which is exactly the null hypothesis 'the
founder carries no information about survivor-set overlap'. It also makes gate B's null the
same permutation as gate A's, which is a feature rather than a coincidence - the entry says
gate B reaches gate A's conclusion 'by a second route', and two routes should differ in their
statistic, not in what they hold fixed.
Two alternatives were considered and rejected, recorded so the choice is visible. (i) One
cross_arm_permutation_test per founder, two chains per arm: the literal reading of the named
function, but n = 2 per arm per founder is below that function's own refusal threshold and
would need a further rule for combining 20 tests, which the entry does not give. (ii) A
different statistic, such as the overlap coefficient: rejected because the entry commits gate
B to Jaccard, and changing the statistic to fit the available function would be the tail
what_this_costs: The two arms are badly unbalanced at R = 2 - 20 same-founder pairs against 760
different-founder pairs - so the same-founder mean is the noisier side by a wide margin and
the observed difference is dominated by its variance. This is a property of R = 2 and not of
the assembly; it is stated here so that a non-significant gate B is not read as evidence of
absence. The permutation null carries the same imbalance, so the p-value remains valid.
Both pair counts are reported beside the statistic.
gate_b_arm_assembly.does_not_change: No threshold, grid, statistic family, tail direction, permutation count or correction moves. This clause only says how the two arms the entry already names are assembled from the chains.

floor_3_has_no_referent_here.added: 2026-11-08, with the gate B clause above and before any chain has been run.
the_silence: Headroom floor 3 says gate B and gate C 'must therefore report, for each null they use, the
number of sets n and an estimate of that first-order variance, and are NOT EVALUABLE if the
two nulls being compared fall in different regimes.' It was written after C-4O, where a

decision.refusal_clause_is_NOT_APPLICABLE: Because each gate uses a single null, the mismatch refusal has nothing to compare. It is recorded per gate as NOT APPLICABLE, with the reason, and is never recorded as passed.
decision.if_a_second_null_is_ever_added: Any future comparison that does set two nulls against each other re-activates the refusal clause as written, with no further amendment needed.

why_not_simply_pass_it: Until 2026-11-08 the aggregator wired this floor as scaling_regime(survivor_sets) against
scaling_regime(survivor_sets) - the same collection twice - so the two regimes were always
equal and the floor could never fire. That is the pathology this project has recorded three
times: C-4 gate B, both C-2R gates, and the C-8 tolerance. 'A check that cannot fail has not
passed.' Recording NOT APPLICABLE says the true thing; recording a pass would say a false one.
A measured reason to keep the distinction sharp: the regime classifier itself misclassifies a
genuinely degenerate null as non-degenerate in roughly one trial in fifteen, measured

The error runs in the permissive direction. A floor with that false-permit rate must not also
be reported as having passed something it never examined.

C-8.name: Frozen-body / random-features null
C-8.question: Does alphabet contraction survive when the representation cannot change - and does the frozen-body head reproduce its own closed-form Laplace posterior?
background: RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 4.1 gives this control two jobs, and they need two different kinds
of rule. As a null it asks whether contraction is purely a readout phenomenon: freeze
model.body at random initialization, train only the head, and the chain becomes regression
in a fixed 256-dimensional random feature space. As a correctness bridge it is the
prerequisite for S-1, preregistered 2026-10-20 at a6d477e - with the body frozen the head is
a GLM whose Laplace posterior is closed form, so 'the analytic prediction and the experiment
must agree. That is a correctness check on the sampler implementation that nothing else in
the design provides.'
The second job is a reproduction check and NOT a hypothesis test. It is recorded below as a
tolerance with no null and no significance level, because attaching a p-value to 'does the
closed-form answer come back out' would be a category error: a reproduction check that
fails is a bug, not a finding, and one that passes is not evidence about the world.
One ambiguity in the plan's wording is resolved here before any run, because the two
readings measure different things. 'Freeze model.body at random initialization and train
only the head each generation' could mean one shared frozen body for the whole chain or a
fresh frozen body per generation. The same sentence says the chain becomes regression in a
FIXED feature space, which forces the first reading. ONE shared frozen body per chain. Under
the second reading the feature space drifts between generations and the Laplace comparison
is ill-posed, so the sampler bridge would not exist at all.
A consequence of that reading, noted so it is not later mistaken for a result: with the body
frozen and the pool fixed, the features are bitwise identical every generation, so
effective_rank(feats) is a constant by construction rather than a measurement. Checking it
is a freeze-leak assertion, not evidence. It is run as a descriptive reproduction check and
is not gated.
Gate A's comparison arm is C-1's intact arm, already published: 7.50 surviving classes with
a 95 percent interval of [5.65, 9.25] over 20 chains at bottleneck 128 across 25
generations, chain seeds 600 to 619, in logs/c1_shuffled_n20.json. That anchor is measured
on the TRAINING pool, so gate A is measured on the training pool too. This is deliberate
and is the one place this control could repeat a defect already paid for: C-4O compared a
covariate from one pool against an outcome defined on another. No n = 20 probe-pool
alphabet anchor exists, and inventing one would mean rerunning C-1. The probe-pool alphabet
is reported beside the gate as a descriptive and carries no verdict.

fixed_in_advance.body: one shared frozen body per chain, at that chain's initialization, requires_grad False AND excluded from the optimizer's parameter list
fixed_in_advance.gate_pool: training pool, because that is the pool the comparison arm is measured on
fixed_in_advance.descriptive_pool: held-out probe pool at probe_seed 9000, reported, not gated

precondition_founder_comparability: ADDED 2026-10-20, after the entry's first commit at c873fcb and BEFORE any gate-A
statistic was computed. What was known when this was added, stated so a reader can
judge it: the frozen-body founder's generation-0 training-pool accuracy, reproduced
twice on this machine, is 0.113525390625 against the full MLP's 0.977294921875, with
chance at 0.0200. A 256-dimensional random feature space cannot fit 4096 random labels
over 50 classes. Gate A's statistic - mean surviving alphabet at generation 25 over 20
chains - had NOT been computed and has still not been.
Why this is an addition rather than a threshold move. It can only cause the control to
refuse; there is no outcome it makes easier to claim. The gates/thresholds.json README
says what a commit buys is that moving a threshold becomes a visible diff instead of a
silent edit, and this is that diff. A reader who thinks it should not have been added
can read the entry at c873fcb and see exactly what changed.
The precondition. Gate A is NOT EVALUABLE unless the frozen-body founder's
generation-0 accuracy falls inside the range the comparison arm's own twenty founders
span: 0.977294921875 to 0.984375, read from logs/c1_shuffled_n20.json. Constant-free by
construction - the criterion is the published arm's own founder spread, not a number
chosen here. On the measurement above the frozen-body founder misses that range by
roughly 120 times its width, so gate A is expected to be refused.
What this costs, recorded now. C-8's null question - is contraction purely a readout
phenomenon - is not answerable by comparing against C-1's intact arm, because the two
arms do not start from comparable models. RESEARCH-PLAN.md:260-262 already asks for a
comparison at matched agreement decay rate rather than matched bottleneck; the same
logic applies here and was not carried into the first version of this entry. A readable
version of the null needs either a wider random feature space that reaches a comparable
generation-0 fit, or a full-MLP comparison arm whose founder is deliberately trained
down to the frozen arm's accuracy. Both are new work and neither is preregistered.
The tolerance below is UNAFFECTED. It compares the frozen-body head against its own
closed-form Laplace posterior on its own features and targets, so a weak founder does
not invalidate it. The sampler correctness bridge, which is why C-8 is a prerequisite
of S-1, therefore survives this precondition intact and remains the reason to build
the control.

A.metric: mean surviving alphabet at generation 25 on the training pool, over 20 frozen-body chains, with a 95 percent bootstrap interval computed the same way C-1 computes its own
A.condition: freezing the representation does not change how far the alphabet contracts
A.fails_if: the frozen-body arm's 95 percent interval does not overlap C-1's intact-arm interval of [5.65, 9.25]
A.meaning_if_failed: the body carries part of the contraction, so contraction is not purely a readout phenomenon; effective rank becomes central to the account and the readout-only reading in RESEARCH-PLAN section 4.1 is wrong
A.meaning_if_passed: contraction is reproduced with a representation that cannot change, so it is a readout phenomenon; the representation-level framing of the contraction result weakens and every statement of it must say that a fixed random feature space suffices to produce it

tolerance_not_a_gate: Statistic: predicted-class agreement on the training pool between the frozen-body head
trained by SGD and the closed-form Laplace posterior mean for the same GLM on the same
features and the same transmitted targets, at generation 1 and at generation 25.
AMENDED 2026-10-20, third commit on this entry. The first version said the tolerance would
be 'the measured accuracy of analysis/laplace_glm.py on its own test problems that have
closed-form answers.' That derivation was measured and does not produce a usable number.
Across four solver settings - default, grad_tol 1e-6, obj_rtol 1e-14, max_iter 500 - at the
production shape D = 256, K = 50, N = 4096, the module's predicted classes differ on 0 of
4096 points, with a worst coefficient spread of 8.524e-10. The solver contributes exactly
nothing at prediction level, so the stated derivation yields a tolerance of 0.000000, and a
tolerance of zero is absurd: 1500-step SGD will never exactly reproduce an exact MAP.
What actually bounds the comparison is the gap between two estimators of the same optimum,
not the precision of either. So the tolerance is derived the way S-1's inertness floor is,
as a comparison with no free constant:
Two frozen-body heads are trained by SGD on identical transmitted data, differing only in
training seed, and their predicted-class disagreement on the training pool is measured at
n = 20 pairs. That is SGD's own run-to-run spread. The Laplace-versus-SGD disagreement
must not exceed it, judged by whether the Laplace-versus-SGD value falls inside the 95
percent interval of the seed-to-seed spread.
Why this is sound and not a loosening. Before this amendment the tolerance had no value at
all, so no outcome was claimable and nothing is made easier. The tolerance's own statistic -
Laplace-versus-SGD predicted-class agreement - has NOT been computed and still has not been;
what was measured is the module's internal reproducibility across solver settings, which is a
different quantity. The seed-spread baseline must be measured and recorded BEFORE the
Laplace comparison is read.
Interpretation, unchanged. Inside the tolerance means the analytic and experimental sides of
the sampler bridge agree and S-1 may proceed. Outside it means something is wrong and S-1
must NOT proceed - but it does not say which of three things is wrong: the GLM
implementation, the adequacy of the Laplace approximation at this curvature, or the freeze
itself. The first cause is excluded before the chain is involved, by
tests/test_laplace_glm.py's closed-form cases.
A floor from the first version is now known to be VACUOUS and is left in place rather than
deleted, so the record shows it. 'NOT EVALUABLE if the Hessian at the MAP is singular to
working precision' can never fire: with prior precision alpha > 0 the Hessian's minimum
eigenvalue is exactly alpha, measured as 1.000e+00 at alpha = 1 and 1.000e-06 at
alpha = 1e-6 on a feature matrix of rank 4 of 8. The rule requires alpha > 0, so the
condition is unreachable. The protection that does work is the module's own: it refuses a
rank-zero feature matrix, where the posterior equals the prior everywhere and an agreement
check would compare the prior with itself and pass whatever the chain did, and it reports
prior_only_directions for rank deficiency short of that rather than refusing a proper
posterior.
headroom: Three floors, each declaring a result NOT EVALUABLE rather than passed.
1. Saturation at generation 1. Gate A is NOT EVALUABLE if the frozen-body arm's alphabet has
already fallen inside C-1's interval at generation 1, before any chaining. Derivation: this
is C-2R's failure exactly - its gates fired at generation 1, where generation 1 is a one-step
student by construction, so the comparison had not yet had the chance to move. An interval
overlap that exists before the chain runs is not evidence about the chain.
2. Singular Hessian. The tolerance is NOT EVALUABLE if the GLM's Hessian at the MAP is
singular to working precision, since a posterior that cannot be formed cannot be compared
against anything. analysis/laplace_glm.py refuses rather than returning a number in that
case, and the refusal is recorded in the log rather than being caught and ignored.
3. Degenerate tolerance baseline. ADDED 2026-10-23, after the tolerance ran, and the
reasoning for adding it afterwards is set out below rather than left implicit. The tolerance
is NOT EVALUABLE at any generation where the seed-spread baseline interval has zero width,
or where the transmitted batch carries fewer than two of the fifty classes.
Derivation, and it is the same shape as floor 1 rather than a new idea. Floor 1 refuses a
comparison that had not yet had the chance to move. This refuses a comparison that can no
longer move. Both are the defect C-4 gate B and C-2R were caught by, and both are
constant-free: the condition is read off the measurement itself, not set to a number chosen
here.
What was measured on 2026-10-23, which is why this floor exists. The hard-label chain the
tolerance runs on is absorbed at a single class from generation 7 onward, so at generation 25
the transmitted batch holds 1 of 50 classes, every trained head predicts that one class on
all 4096 points, and the n = 20 seed-spread baseline is 0.000000 with an interval of
[0.000000, 0.000000]. The Laplace-versus-SGD disagreement is also 0.000000, so under the rule
as previously worded 0.0 <= 0.0 <= 0.0 reads as WITHIN and the runner prints that S-1 may
proceed. That verdict is empty: SGD's negative log posterior there is 37.917308 against the
MAP's 19.761440, an excess of 18.16 nats, so the two estimators are demonstrably at different
points in weight space while the statistic reads exact agreement. A statistic that cannot
fail has not passed.
Why this is an addition and not a threshold move, judged the same way the
founder-comparability precondition was. It can only cause a refusal; there is no outcome it
makes easier to claim. It does not touch the generation-1 reading, which is the one
informative checkpoint and which fell inside its baseline on its own terms
(logs/c8_tolerance.json, 0.140625 inside [0.136609, 0.190407], 40 of 50 classes present).
Its effect is to remove a second checkpoint that was never evidence, which makes the
sampler bridge rest on one measurement rather than appearing to rest on two.
Consequence for S-1, stated so it is not discovered later. With generation 25 refused, C-8's
tolerance supplies ONE informative comparison. Whether one is sufficient for the bridge is
not decided here and is not decided by this control. S-1's own
precondition_sampler_exactness is the check that does not depend on the chain reaching any
particular generation, and it is the one that should carry that weight.
combination: Gate A and the tolerance are independent and are reported separately. The control does not
produce a single PASSED or FAILED verdict, because its two jobs answer different questions
and merging them would hide which one moved.
Gate A carries the scientific consequence. The tolerance carries a go / no-go for S-1 and
nothing else. A failing tolerance does NOT invalidate gate A: whether the alphabet contracts
with a frozen body is a measurement that stands whether or not the Laplace comparison agrees.
The reverse also holds.
sanity_check: The founder must reproduce the memorization accuracy the existing logs record for its seed;
C-1's intact arm records per-seed founder accuracies between 0.977294921875 and 0.984375 for
chain seeds 600 to 619, and the frozen-body arm uses the same founders.
The features must be bitwise identical across all 25 generations within a chain, checked with
exact equality and not a tolerance. Any difference means the freeze leaked and no number from
that chain is used.
No parameter outside model.head may change between generations. Checked by comparing the
body's state_dict before and after each generation.
logs/c1_shuffled_n20.json is read for its comparison interval and never rewritten.
verdict_if_failed: Gate A failing means the frozen-body arm contracts differently from the full MLP, so the
representation is doing part of the work. The contraction result keeps its representation-level
reading, effective rank stays central, and C-7's linear null becomes more informative rather
than less.
verdict_if_passed: Gate A passing means a fixed random feature space reproduces the contraction. The project's
contraction result is then a readout phenomenon, which narrows it: every statement of it must
say that no representational change is required to produce it. This is the outcome that costs
the most, and it is recorded here before the run so that it cannot later be presented as a
neutral finding.
final_status_2026_10_27: Gate A is recorded NOT EVALUABLE and is closed. It is not amended and will not be rerun. The
founder-comparability precondition refused it as predicted (logs/c8_frozen_body.txt: 0 of 20
frozen-body founders inside C-1's range). Its readable successor is the separate entry C-8b.
The tolerance stands as recorded, informative at generation 1 only (floor 3).

C-8b.name: Frozen random-body learner from a shared, trained founder
C-8b.question: Given an identical founder, does a learner whose representation cannot change contract the alphabet as far as the full MLP does?
background: C-8 gate A is NOT EVALUABLE because its frozen-body founders reached 0.108 to 0.126 accuracy against
C-1's 0.977 to 0.984, so the founder and the learner changed together. Two repairs were probed in
scratch on 2026-10-27 and rejected (not in logs/, unverified). Widening the random body reaches C-1's
accuracy only near h = 8192 and its founder is far softer (entropy 2.08 against 0.24 nats), so
accuracy matching does not match the transmitted targets. Training the full MLP down to 0.11 needs
per-seed step tuning, a forking path. C-8b instead holds the founder fixed by identity: generation 0
is C-1's own founder for each pool seed, and only the students differ.
DISCLOSED: chain seeds 600, 601 and 602 were run in that scratch spike before this entry was
committed (frozen-arm generation-25 alphabets 1, 1, 2). They cannot be replaced, because the arm must
share C-1's pools and chain seeds. They are therefore run and reported, but EXCLUDED from the gate:
the verdict is read on the 17 unseen chains, 603 to 619, against C-1's own 17 chains on the same
seeds, recomputed from logs/c1_shuffled_n20.json.

fixed_in_advance.pool_seeds: C-1's pool seed for each chain, read from logs/c1_shuffled_n20.json
fixed_in_advance.founder: C-1's recipe exactly: torch.manual_seed(seed), make_pool(seed, noise), full MLP, 3000 steps
fixed_in_advance.students: head reinitialised and retrained each generation on ONE frozen random body per chain, as C-8's runner does it
fixed_in_advance.comparison_arm: C-1 intact, restricted to the same 17 chain seeds, recomputed from logs/c1_shuffled_n20.json with C-1's own bootstrap
fixed_in_advance.descriptive_companion: the same chains with the FOUNDER's own body frozen after generation 0; reported, never gated

precondition_founder_identity: Every founder's memorisation accuracy must equal the founder accuracy logged for that seed in
logs/c1_shuffled_n20.json, by float equality. Any mismatch means the harness has drifted from C-1,
and gate A is NOT EVALUABLE.

A.metric: mean surviving alphabet at generation 25 on the training pool over the 17 gated chains, 95 percent bootstrap interval computed as C-1 computes its own
A.comparison: C-1 intact over the same 17 chain seeds, same bootstrap

outcomes.deeper: frozen interval entirely below the intact interval: a fixed random readout suffices and contracts further, so learning the body slows contraction
outcomes.shallower: frozen interval entirely above: the body carries part of the contraction, and effective rank stays central to the account
outcomes.overlap: freezing the representation does not change contraction resolvably at n = 17; contraction is reproduced by a readout alone

A.derivation: Two-sided interval overlap against the comparison arm's own interval, no free constant. Two-sided because C-8's one-sided meanings assumed a direction that the disclosed spike contradicts.

headroom: 1. Saturation at generation 1: gate A is NOT EVALUABLE if the frozen arm's generation-1 interval
already overlaps the comparison arm's generation-25 interval (C-8 floor 1, carried over).
2. Shuffled floor: if the frozen arm's interval overlaps C-1's shuffled-arm interval, only 'deeper'
may be stated, worded as 'to the floor'; depth beyond it is not read. Mean alphabet over generations
1 to 25 is reported beside it.
3. Fidelity covariate, not gated: generation-1 predicted-class agreement with the founder for both
arms, intervals over chains. The intact arm is recomputed for generation 1 only, and its generation-1
alphabets must equal C-1's logged sizes, or that recomputation is discarded. Any 'deeper' statement
quotes both agreements beside it, because a frozen learner that copies worse would also contract
faster for that reason alone.
sanity_check: Features bitwise identical across generations within a chain; the frozen body's state_dict unchanged
after every generation; logs/c1_shuffled_n20.json read and never written. The log declares
control = 'C-8b' at top level so ci/check_gate_ordering.py can match it.
verdict_if_failed: The arm reads 'deeper' or 'shallower' as registered above; neither is a failure of the experiment.
verdict_if_passed: Overlap: contraction does not depend resolvably on whether the representation can change, at n = 17.
